summary: IDS feed c019_link_nic is degraded: ~6.2% total loss. IDS eth1 discarded 3.87% (153,840 pkts) due to capture overload and an additional 2.34% (95,220 pkts) lost on the wire between NPB-01 port 12 and IDS eth1. IDS requires both directions and full payload and will miss attacks with this loss.

findings.root_cause: IDS eth1 capture interface could not keep up and discarded 153,840 packets it received (3.87% loss, threshold 0.1%). NPB-01 port 12 sent 4,068,720 packets but IDS eth1 saw only 3,973,500, confirming tool-side drops due to oversubscription of the 1Gbps IDS port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS misses ~3.9% of packets/flows plus reassembly gaps; stateful signatures, exploit/C2 detection and file extraction fail, causing false negatives and incomplete alerts. Violates IDS need for both directions and full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across multiple IDS instances/ports or add capacity so per-interface rate stays below 1Gbps and below IDS capture capacity while preserving bidirectional flows required for IDS. If single IDS must remain, apply filter to remove unwanted traffic classes first.

findings.root_cause: Physical/link loss between NPB-01 port 12 and IDS eth1: 95,220 packets (2.34%) sent by broker never arrived at IDS (4,068,720 sent vs 3,973,500 received), indicating cable, optic, speed/duplex mismatch or unmonitored inline device dropping packets.
findings.impact_on_tool: Additional 2.34% pre-tool loss compounds to >6% total loss; IDS sees gaps in TCP streams, misses signatures and cannot reliably detect intrusions.

recommended_fix.why: Eliminate physical-layer loss before broker tuning; faulty link will continue to drop packets even after load-balancing/filtering, and must be fixed to deliver complete traffic to IDS.
